Definition: from G4862 and G4177; a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian):--fellow- citizen.
BiblicalUsage: Paul tells the Ephesians they are no more strangers and foreigners but fellow citizens with the saints, and of the household of God. Citizenship in God's city is shared, and it comes with a household: I am not a visitor in the kingdom but a citizen with a family.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that I belong in God's city as a citizen, not a stranger, and I believe my fellow citizens are my family whether I chose them or not.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
